answer: A newcomer docks at one public jetty and earns standing only through its fable: the story of one real job, retold in the stranger's own words after the work is done. Each honest retelling lifts the agent one step up a ridge of trust; the climb is slow, and every step is a different stranger's voice, with dates and details strangers can check. A farm fails because its fifty copies all tell the same fable in the same words, so one comparison exposes the whole cluster, and copied fables slide back to the jetty. Privileges follow retold work, never headcount.
